network.overall_strategy: An experimentally anchored surface-cyanosulfidic network is used as the backbone: C3 oxygenates converge on an acetone hub, acetone is converted to an acetone-cyanohydrin hub, and the main resolved branch proceeds through thioamide, alpha-hydroxynitrile, and aminonitrile intermediates to valine. A second literature-anchored but mechanistically unresolved branch to valine via 2-amino-4-methylpentanenitrile is included as a condensed alternative. To provide 10 distinct pathways without inventing many unsupported reactions, the pathways are enumerated as distinct entry-to-target routes through shared hubs, with only one explicitly speculative upstream triose-provisioning step added. All mapped chemistry is assigned to surface pools because that is where Patel et al. (2015) place valine-forming cyanosulfidic chemistry. Valine is represented without fixed stereochemistry because prebiotic production is expected to be racemic.

reactions.name: Formose-type triose generation of dihydroxyacetone

conditions.other: anoxic evaporitic pool; wet-dry concentration; mild basicity permits aldol and isomerization chemistry

reactions.mechanism: Net C1+C2 aldol chemistry gives a C3 triose manifold, followed by keto-enol isomerization to the ketose dihydroxyacetone.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative upstream provisioning step. The curated review notes that dihydroxyacetone and hydroxyacetone needed for the valine network could arise from formose-type or related prebiotic carbonyl chemistry, but Patel et al. (2015) did not directly demonstrate this valine-specific net conversion. It is included to connect the experimentally anchored cyanosulfidic route to simpler feedstocks while acknowledging that C3 sugar availability remains an open question (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Dihydroxyacetone reductive deoxygenation to acetone

conditions.other: anoxic cyanosulfidic pool; dissolved sulfide present; water byproduct omitted from graph

reactions.mechanism: Cu/H2S-mediated reductive deoxygenation removes oxygenated substituents from the triose, collapsing it to acetone.
reactions.reasoning: This upstream entry into the valine network is explicitly reported under surface cyanosulfidic conditions: dihydroxyacetone is reductively deoxygenated to acetone by copper and sulfide (Patel et al., 2015). The review notes uncertainty about prebiotic copper availability, but the reaction itself is experimentally supported.

reactions.name: Hydroxyacetone reductive deoxygenation to acetone

conditions.other: anoxic cyanosulfidic pool; dissolved sulfide present; water byproduct omitted from graph

reactions.mechanism: Cu/H2S-mediated reductive deoxygenation of the hydroxymethyl substituent gives acetone.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) explicitly identify hydroxyacetone as an alternative entry feedstock that is reduced to acetone in the same surface cyanosulfidic regime. This reaction creates the second experimentally anchored route into the acetone hub.

reactions.name: Acetone cyanohydrin formation

conditions.other: HCN-rich anoxic pool; near-neutral to mildly basic CN- availability

reactions.mechanism: Cyanide adds to the acetone carbonyl, and protonation of the alkoxide yields the tertiary cyanohydrin.
reactions.reasoning: Classical cyanohydrin formation from acetone is one of the central experimentally supported steps in the Patel et al. (2015) valine sequence. It introduces the nitrile carbon that later maps to the amino-acid carboxylate.

reactions.name: Thioamide formation from acetone cyanohydrin
reactions.mechanism: Sulfide adds to the nitrile and proton transfers furnish the corresponding thioamide.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) report conversion of acetone cyanohydrin to the thioamide with H2S. This activation step is chemically important because the thioamide is the substrate for the key C-C bond-forming rearrangement.

reactions.name: Cu/H2S-mediated branched chain extension to hydroxynitrile

conditions.other: anoxic cyanosulfidic pool with sulfide present; sulfur redox byproducts omitted from graph

reactions.mechanism: A Cu/H2S-mediated reductive rearrangement incorporates an additional cyanide-derived carbon and reorganizes the thioamide to the branched C5 alpha-hydroxynitrile.
reactions.reasoning: This is the decisive branched-skeleton-forming step directly supported by Patel et al. (2015). The review emphasizes that the detailed radical versus polar mechanism remains unresolved, so the transformation is represented at the network level while omitting sulfur byproducts such as disulfane.

reactions.name: Amination to valine aminonitrile

conditions.other: NH3-rich concentrated surface pool; water byproduct omitted from graph

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia substitutes for the alpha-hydroxyl group to give the Strecker-type aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) support amination of 2-hydroxy-3-methylbutanenitrile to 2-amino-3-methylbutanenitrile. This is the direct pre-hydrolysis precursor to valine in the experimentally resolved main branch.

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of valine aminonitrile to valine

conditions.other: hydrating phase of a cyanosulfidic pool; ammonia byproduct omitted from graph

reactions.mechanism: Hydrolysis of the aminonitrile proceeds through amide-like hydration to the carboxylic acid, giving valine.
reactions.reasoning: Hydrolysis of the valine aminonitrile to valine is experimentally supported in Patel et al. (2015). Because no enantioselective step is present in the network, the prebiotic product is best interpreted as racemic valine; the origin of L-enrichment remains unresolved in the review.

reactions.name: Condensed alternative homologation to C6 aminonitrile

conditions.other: anoxic cyanosulfidic pool; condensed net representation of an unresolved multistep homologation branch from acetone-derived nitrile chemistry; multiple HCN equivalents may be involved

reactions.mechanism: Net sequence of one or more further cyanide homologations, sulfide activation, Cu-mediated reductive rearrangement, and amination converts the acetone-cyanohydrin manifold to a C6 aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: The curated review states that Patel et al. (2015) identified a parallel hydroxyacetone-derived route to valine passing through 2-amino-4-methylpentanenitrile, but it does not resolve the intervening stepwise chemistry. This reaction is therefore explicitly speculative in microscopic detail. Placing the branch after acetone cyanohydrin is chemically justified because hydroxyacetone first enters the validated acetone chemistry, and acetone cyanohydrin is the first established nitrile-bearing intermediate from which additional homologation is plausible (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Hydrolysis and chain shortening of C6 aminonitrile to valine

conditions.other: hydrating surface pool; apparent chain-shortening accompanies hydrolysis; ammonia byproduct omitted from graph

reactions.mechanism: Net nitrile hydrolysis with concomitant one-carbon loss converts the C6 aminonitrile to the C5 amino acid valine.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) and the curated review support conversion of 2-amino-4-methylpentanenitrile to valine, but the review explicitly flags the chain-shortening mechanism during hydrolysis as unresolved. The step is therefore included as experimentally reported at the network level, with mechanistic caution.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Strategically coherent and literature-shaped, but this route combines the only explicitly speculative upstream step with several conservation failures. rxn_001 is balanced but only loosely anchored as a surface formose-type entry. rxn_002 is unbalanced; the checker shows a formal O2 deficit, which indicates missing redox bookkeeping rather than a credible standalone deoxygenation. The downstream main branch matches the Patel-style valine logic, but rxn_006 is a major unbalanced chain-extension step, rxn_007 should release H2O, and rxn_008 should consume 2 H2O and release NH3. Surface assignment is broadly acceptable, but the encoded chemistry is not yet conservation-valid.
suggestions: Either justify rxn_001 with explicit surface-formose conditions or treat dihydroxyacetone as an imported feedstock instead of generating it here.
Rewrite rxn_002 with explicit Cu/H2S redox participants and coproducts; the current one-substrate deoxygenation is not conservation-valid.
Add missing sulfur/nitrogen byproducts for rxn_006, ideally including an explicit disulfane (H2S2) node if that is the intended sulfur sink.
Correct rxn_007 to produce H2O and rxn_008 to consume 2 H2O and release NH3.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the literature-aligned dihydroxyacetone main branch, and the intermediate sequence acetone -> cyanohydrin -> thioamide -> hydroxynitrile -> aminonitrile -> valine is coherent. However, the encoded stoichiometry is not valid. rxn_002 is unbalanced and omits the Cu/H2S redox bookkeeping, rxn_006 is the weakest step and lacks explicit sulfur/nitrogen redox byproducts, rxn_007 should generate H2O, and rxn_008 should be written with 2 H2O in and NH3 out. Good conceptual match to the reviewed chemistry, but poor conservation accuracy.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_002 with explicit redox participants/coproducts instead of a bare deoxygenation.
Add the missing sulfur redox products and any nitrogen byproducts to rxn_006, or split it into smaller literature-grounded steps.
Correct rxn_007 to mol_012 + mol_004 -> mol_013 + mol_001.
Correct rxn_008 to mol_013 + 2 mol_001 -> mol_015 + mol_004.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Hydroxyacetone entry is consistent with the reviewed surface cyanosulfidic chemistry, and the route coherently joins the established acetone hub. The pathway is still not valid as encoded because rxn_003 omits the necessary redox bookkeeping for deoxygenation, rxn_006 is unbalanced and mechanistically under-specified, rxn_007 should release H2O, and rxn_008 needs extra water plus NH3 release. Literature alignment is decent for the route logic, but the stoichiometric implementation is incomplete.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_003 with explicit Cu/H2S redox participants and coproducts rather than a one-substrate deoxygenation.
Add missing sulfur/nitrogen byproducts to rxn_006 or decompose it into stepwise transformations.
Correct rxn_007 to mol_012 + mol_004 -> mol_013 + mol_001.
Correct rxn_008 to mol_013 + 2 mol_001 -> mol_015 + mol_004.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Best encoded pathway. From acetone onward the sequence matches the main Patel-type cyanosulfidic valine logic and all steps fit naturally in a surface pool setting. The main defect is conservation: rxn_006 is badly unbalanced and likely needs explicit sulfur redox byproducts and better stepwise specification, while rxn_007 and rxn_008 are close but still miswritten stoichiometrically. Because this branch reaches valine through the chemically appropriate C5 aminonitrile, it remains more credible than the alternative C6 branch.
suggestions: Add explicit sulfur redox byproducts or split rxn_006 into smaller experimentally grounded steps.
Correct rxn_007 to mol_012 + mol_004 -> mol_013 + mol_001.
Correct rxn_008 to mol_013 + 2 mol_001 -> mol_015 + mol_004.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Reasonable subpath from acetone cyanohydrin, with strong literature support for thioamide formation and the expected downstream intermediate identities. However, rxn_006 is the key weak link and fails deterministic conservation, while rxn_007 and rxn_008 are chemically familiar but stoichiometrically incomplete. This makes the branch conceptually sound but not valid as encoded.
suggestions: Add explicit sulfur redox products and better mechanistic specification to rxn_006.
Correct rxn_007 to include H2O as product.
Correct rxn_008 to include 2 H2O as reactants and NH3 as product.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This shortened route depends almost entirely on the problematic chain-extension step. Even though the intermediates are appropriate for valine synthesis, rxn_006 is unbalanced with no simple single-species fix, so the pathway is not conservation-valid. rxn_007 and rxn_008 are chemically conventional transformations but still need explicit H2O/NH3 bookkeeping.
suggestions: Re-specify rxn_006 with explicit sulfur and nitrogen byproducts, or break it into smaller validated reactions.
Correct rxn_007 to mol_012 + mol_004 -> mol_013 + mol_001.
Correct rxn_008 to mol_013 + 2 mol_001 -> mol_015 + mol_004.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Chemically this is the cleanest terminal segment: hydroxynitrile amination followed by aminonitrile hydrolysis is textbook and literature-supported. The issue is specification rather than concept. rxn_007 should be mol_012 + mol_004 -> mol_013 + mol_001, and rxn_008 should be mol_013 + 2 mol_001 -> mol_015 + mol_004. As written, both violate atom balance, so the pathway cannot be considered fully valid even though its chemistry is credible.
suggestions: Rewrite rxn_007 as mol_012 + mol_004 -> mol_013 + mol_001.
Rewrite rxn_008 as mol_013 + 2 mol_001 -> mol_015 + mol_004.
Add reaction-level citation or condition notes for these terminal amination and hydrolysis steps.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The alternative C6 branch is not convincing valine chemistry. rxn_009 compresses an unresolved homologation into a single unbalanced reaction, and rxn_010 attempts to convert a C6 aminonitrile directly to C5 valine without any carbon-containing coproduct. Hydrolysis of 2-amino-4-methylpentanenitrile would ordinarily give a C6 amino acid, not valine, unless a separate chain-shortening mechanism is explicitly defined. The hydroxyacetone-to-acetone entry is literature-aligned but cannot rescue the branch.
suggestions: Remove this as a valine branch unless you can specify a balanced, stepwise chain-shortening mechanism with explicit carbon-loss products.
If mol_014 is intended to hydrolyze normally, reconsider whether the product should instead be a C6 amino acid rather than valine.
Repair rxn_003 stoichiometry if the hydroxyacetone entry is retained.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Acetone and cyanohydrin entry are fine, but the downstream alternative branch does not establish valine chemistry. rxn_009 is an unbalanced unexplained leap to a C6 aminonitrile, and rxn_010 is an unbalanced hydrolysis/chain-shortening step with no carbon-containing coproduct and no defensible mechanism for producing valine.
suggestions: Replace the condensed rxn_009 with documented intermediate steps or omit the branch.
Do not treat rxn_010 as simple hydrolysis; specify the carbon-containing coproduct and chain-shortening mechanism if valine is truly intended.
Retain the acetone/cyanohydrin entry only if the downstream chemistry is corrected.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: As a two-step branch, this is not chemically defensible for valine. rxn_009 is an unbalanced and mechanistically unexplained leap to a C6 aminonitrile, and rxn_010 is an unbalanced hydrolysis/chain-shortening step that lacks any carbon-containing coproduct and conflicts with the expected product identity. This branch should not be counted as a valid valine pathway in its current form.
suggestions: Delete or fully re-specify this branch; as written it is not a valid valine pathway.
Introduce explicit carbon-loss chemistry and coproducts if converting mol_014 to valine is intended.
Provide literature-grounded stepwise intermediates instead of the single-step rxn_009 leap.

evaluation.network_feedback: Connected network with consistent IDs and no isolated subgraphs. Only rxn_001, rxn_004, and rxn_005 are balanced as written; the other 7 reactions fail the deterministic conservation check. The main acetone -> acetone cyanohydrin -> thioamide -> hydroxynitrile -> aminonitrile -> valine branch is strategically coherent and aligns well with the Patel et al. surface cyanosulfidic literature, while the all-surface environmental assignment is broadly appropriate and representing valine without fixed stereochemistry is sensible for prebiotic chemistry. However, rxn_002 and rxn_003 show formal O2 deficits in the balance check and need explicit Cu/H2S redox participants and coproducts rather than one-substrate deoxygenations; rxn_006 is a major unbalanced chain-extension step and likely needs explicit sulfur redox byproducts such as H2S2 plus better stepwise specification; rxn_007 should release H2O; rxn_008 should be mol_013 + 2 mol_001 -> mol_015 + mol_004; and rxn_009-rxn_010 are not acceptable valine chemistry as written, with rxn_010 especially requiring a carbon-containing coproduct and a defended chain-shortening mechanism. Literature alignment is strong for the main branch and weak for the condensed C6 branch. Overall the network is chemically suggestive but not conservation-valid, so it is not approved.
